conceptZh: 豬探長舉著超大放大鏡辦案，鏡片把他的眼睛放大成爆笑巨眼；他湊得太近撞到太陽，太陽被壓成直立的圓角方塊，脫手的放大鏡橫飛過來「喀」一聲卡進中間變成那一橫，合成「日」。
object: a chubby glossy toy sun ball with a calm smiling face, and a stout cartoon detective pig with an oversized magnifying glass
morph: the sun squashes into an upright rounded rectangle while the flying magnifying glass snaps across its middle and smooths into the single horizontal stroke of 日
creativeAngle: 第一次為「日」補上 prompt。用孩子喜歡的豬探長開場，放大鏡巨眼是笑點，也自然帶出「撞一下→壓扁→橫桿插進來」的因果，不靠老套的果凍登場。語音詞選「生日」，日固定念ㄖˋ、生固定念ㄕㄥ，沒有破音風險。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid light-cream background. Centered stands a chubby glossy toy sun: a round tangerine ball with a calm smiling face. A stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker hat and a tiny trench coat waddles in from the left, holding a magnifying glass far too big for him. From 0.6 to 2.2 seconds he leans in to inspect the sun and, seen through the lens, his one eye balloons to a comically enormous size and blinks twice while the rest of him stays small. Hold that silly pose for a beat. At 2.6 seconds he leans one step too close, bonks the sun with the lens rim, and the sun squashes with a soft jelly wobble into an upright rounded rectangle of saturated vermilion. The magnifying glass pops out of his hands, spins once through the air, and snaps horizontally across the middle of that rectangle with a satisfying click, its rim and handle smoothing into one clean straight stroke. The detective pig tips his hat, very pleased with himself, and hops out of frame to the left by 4.6 seconds. By 5.0 seconds the shape has resolved into one correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 日 in saturated vermilion, perfectly centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height with generous margins on all sides, its outer box and single middle bar crisp, straight and clearly separated. From 5.0 to 8.0 seconds the frame holds completely still on 日 with nothing else moving in the shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast but not neon colors, no dark or moody grading. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「日、日、生日」, using the reading ㄖˋ for 日 both times and in the word. Speak the first 日 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 生日 around 5.6 seconds during the still hold, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep the bonk and the click soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not appear as imagery. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 日: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 「日」像太陽照出暖暖日光，長短手的玩具機器人想遮陽，卻被自己的長手拍肩，轉頭找了半天。
object: A solid orange-red 日 glyph shining warm sunlight beside a boxy toy robot assembled from mismatched parts.
morph: Begin with the complete, correctly formed glyph. Its shape remains fixed while its sunlight motivates the robot’s self-tapping shade gag; the lighting settles into a flat, crisp final reading view.
creativeAngle: 改用完整的「日」直接表現太陽與日光，不再壓扁太陽或拼接筆畫。機器人過長的手繞到背後拍到自己，誤以為有人叫它，最後才把長手折成遮陽棚。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one locked-off frontal shot. On a light cream background, place one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 日 precisely at center, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use saturated solid orange-red strokes: an upright rectangular enclosure and one straight horizontal middle stroke joining its left and right sides, with two clearly open cream-colored interior spaces. Keep this geometry intact throughout. The glyph acts as a sun, casting gentle warm light toward the lower-left margin without adding rays, a face, or decorations to its strokes.

The sole animated lead is an original boxy toy robot assembled from visibly mismatched parts: a squat turquoise torso, a mustard square head, mismatched toy feet, one stubby arm and one conspicuously long segmented arm. Its personality is earnestly overconfident. Stage it entirely beside the glyph, with enough separation that its gestures never cross the strokes. No additional props or supporting cast.

At the opening, the robot happily basks in the glyph’s sunlight, then squints and attempts to shade its eyes with its stubby arm. The hand cannot reach its forehead; it stretches onto tiptoe and pauses, baffled. Around 1.3 seconds, it confidently swings its much longer arm overhead. The arm overshoots, bends behind its head, and softly taps its own opposite shoulder. The robot immediately swivels its head to investigate; its attached hand follows and taps again, making it turn back with an exaggerated puzzled double-take. Let this tiny chase read clearly rather than spinning rapidly. By 3.3 seconds, the robot spots its own hand, freezes in sheepish recognition, then deliberately folds the long elbow so the broad palm becomes a perfectly useful sunshade above its eyes. It gives one satisfied nod and waddles out through the left edge by 4.7 seconds, still shading itself.

By 4.8 seconds, the directional sunlight has gently settled into even studio illumination. Hold only the crisp, centered 日 completely still through 8.0 seconds, preserving its solid color, clean interior spaces and full margins. Use chunky molded toy materials, soft shadows and bright restrained colors, with no flashing or blown-out highlights.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「日、日、日光」. Pronounce 日 as ㄖˋ throughout. Speak the first 日 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.3 seconds, and 日光 around 5.5 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly visible in the final hold. Use natural pauses and stop after the word. Add only quiet toy-joint creaks and two soft shoulder taps beneath the voice; no music. The vocabulary is audio only. Keep 日 as the only on-screen writing, with no subtitles, other text, logos, watermarks or clutter. Use only the original stylized toy cast and objects described.
